mainEntity.name: Is it normal for a dental implant to feel slightly different after many years?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is not uncommon for patients to notice subtle changes in how a dental implant feels over time — for example, minor wear on the crown surface may alter how the bite feels slightly. However, any sense of movement, rocking, or instability is not normal and should be assessed professionally. Similarly, changes in gum appearance or comfort around the implant are worth discussing at your next appointment or sooner if they are persistent.

mainEntity.name: Can a loose crown on a dental implant be fixed without removing the implant?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, yes. If the movement is limited to the crown or abutment component — rather than the implant fixture itself — this is often a straightforward procedure. The crown or abutment can be re-secured or replaced without disturbing the underlying implant post. A clinical examination is needed to confirm precisely where the looseness originates, so it is important not to assume the cause without professional assessment.

mainEntity.name: Does teeth grinding (bruxism) affect dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bruxism can place significant repetitive stress on dental implants, the surrounding bone, and the crown. Over time, this may contribute to bone loss, loosening of components, or wear of the crown itself. If you are aware that you grind your teeth, it is important to discuss this with your dental team before and after implant placement. A custom-made nightguard may be recommended to help distribute forces more evenly and protect the implant.

Treatment for peri-implantitis depends on the stage of the condition and is determined following clinical and radiographic assessment. Early-stage peri-implant mucositis may respond well to professional cleaning and improved home hygiene. More advanced peri-implantitis involving bone loss may require more intensive professional treatment, which in some cases involves surgical access to clean the affected area. Treatment outcomes vary between individuals, and no specific outcome can be guaranteed without individual clinical assessment.

mainEntity.name: Can dental implants fail after many years of working well?

acceptedAnswer.text: Although it is less common than early failure, dental implants can encounter problems after an extended period of successful function. Long-term issues are often related to the development of peri-implantitis, changes in bone density, systemic health changes, or cumulative effects of habits such as bruxism. This is one reason why regular long-term monitoring of dental implants is recommended, even when they are functioning comfortably and the patient has no concerns.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an implant fixture loosening and a crown becoming loose?

acceptedAnswer.text: These are two distinct issues with different clinical implications. A loose crown or abutment means the prosthetic components attached to the implant have become detached or unstable — this is relatively common and generally straightforward to address. A loose implant fixture, where the titanium post itself is moving within the bone, is a more significant finding that typically indicates compromised osseointegration or significant bone loss. Only a clinical examination can distinguish between the two.
